claim: Ectopic Cushing's syndrome due to ectopic ACTH&CRH-secreting by pheochromocytoma is extremely rare and can be fatal if not properly diagnosed.
source: Ectopic Cushing's syndrome due to ectopic ACTH&CRH-secreting by pheochromocytoma is extremely rare and can be fatal if not properly diagnosed.
evidence: This is a general statement about the rarity and severity of the condition, drawing from established medical knowledge.

claim: A total of 16 cell types in the tumor microenvironment were identified by unbiased cell clustering of single-cell transcriptomic profiles from all specimens.
source: A total of 16 cell types in the tumor microenvironment were identified by unbiased cell clustering of single-cell transcriptomic profiles from all specimens.
evidence: This claim is supported by the scRNA-seq data analysis performed in the study.

claim: A novel multi-functionally chromaffin-like cell type with high expression of both POMC (the precursor of ACTH) and CRH was identified, called ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte.
source: Notably, we identified a novel multi-functionally chromaffin-like cell type with high expression of both POMC (the precursor of ACTH) and CRH, called ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by scRNA-seq data analysis.

claim: The secretion of ACTH had a direct effect on the adrenal gland to produce cortisol, while the secretion of CRH can indirectly stimulate the secretion of ACTH from the anterior pituitary.
source: We hypothesized that the molecular mechanism of the rare case harbor Cushing's syndrome is due to the identified novel tumor cell type, that is, the secretion of ACTH had a direct effect on the adrenal gland to produce cortisol, while the secretion of CRH can indirectly stimulate the secretion of ACTH from the anterior pituitary.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the data and established knowledge of the HPA axis.

claim: GAL is a new potential marker co-expressed with ACTH and CRH that might be involved in the regulation of ACTH secretion.
source: Besides, a new potential marker (GAL) co-expressed with ACTH and CRH might be involved in the regulation of ACTH secretion.
evidence: This is based on the observation of GAL expression in the scRNA-seq data and speculation about its function.

claim: Immunohistochemistry results confirmed the multi-functionally chromaffin-like properties with positive staining for CRH, POMC, ACTH, GAL, TH, and CgA.
source: The immunohistochemistry results confirmed its multi-functionally chromaffin-like properties with positive staining for CRH, POMC, ACTH, GAL, TH, and CgA.
evidence: This is supported by IHC experimental data.

claim: About 80% of CS cases are due to ACTH secretion by a pituitary adenoma.
source: About 80% of CS cases are due to ACTH secretion by a pituitary adenoma, about 20% are due to ACTH secretion by nonpituitary tumors (ectopic ACTH syndrome [EAS]), and 1% are caused by corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)-secreting tumors (Alexandraki and Grossman, 2010; Ejaz et al., 2011; Ballav et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: About 20% of CS cases are due to ACTH secretion by nonpituitary tumors (ectopic ACTH syndrome [EAS]).
source: About 80% of CS cases are due to ACTH secretion by a pituitary adenoma, about 20% are due to ACTH secretion by nonpituitary tumors (ectopic ACTH syndrome [EAS]), and 1% are caused by corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)-secreting tumors (Alexandraki and Grossman, 2010; Ejaz et al., 2011; Ballav et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: 1% of CS cases are caused by corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)-secreting tumors.
source: About 80% of CS cases are due to ACTH secretion by a pituitary adenoma, about 20% are due to ACTH secretion by nonpituitary tumors (ectopic ACTH syndrome [EAS]), and 1% are caused by corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)-secreting tumors (Alexandraki and Grossman, 2010; Ejaz et al., 2011; Ballav et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Only 2.5–5% of all EAS are caused by a pheochromocytoma.
source: Most EAS tumors (~60%) are more common intrathoracic tumors, only 2.5–5% of all EAS are caused by a pheochromocytoma (Alexandraki and Grossman, 2010; Isidori et al., 2006; Ilias et al., 2005; Aniszewski et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: By 2020, only two cases with pheochromocytoma secreted both ACTH and CRH were reported.
source: By 2020, only two cases with pheochromocytoma secreted both ACTH and CRH were reported (Elliott et al., 2021; O'Brien et al., 1992; Jessop et al., 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous case reports.

claim: Cushing's syndrome has an annual incidence of about 0.2–5.0 per million.
source: Cushing's syndrome (CS) is a rare disorder caused by long-term exposure to excessive glucocorticoids, with an annual incidence of about 0.2–5.0 per million (Lacroix et al., 2015; Newell-Price et al., 2006; Lindholm et al., 2001; Steffensen et al., 2010; Bolland et al., 2011; Valassi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to epidemiological studies.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing can examine the expression profiles of a single cell and is recognized as the gold standard for defining cell states and phenotypes.
source: Currently, single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) can examine the expression profiles of a single cell and is recognized as the gold standard for defining cell states and phenotypes (Tang et al., 2009; Tammela and Sage, 2020; Kolodziejczyk et al., 2015; Patel et al., 2014; Tirosh et al., 2016b; Tirosh et al., 2016a; Puram et al., 2017; Venteicher et al., 2017; Young et al., 2018; Bernard et al., 2019; Segerstolpe et al., 2016; Reichert and Rustgi, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature on scRNA-seq methodology.

claim: scRNA-seq can reveal the presence of rare and novel unique cell types, such as CFTR-expressing pulmonary ionocytes on lung airway epithelia.
source: It can reveal the presence of rare and novel unique cell types, such as CFTR-expressing pulmonary ionocytes on lung airway epithelia (Montoro et al., 2018; Plasschaert et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies that used scRNA-seq to discover novel cell types.

claim: scRNA-seq provides an unbiased method to better understand the diversity of immune cells in the complex tumor microenvironment.
source: It also provides an unbiased method to better understand the diversity of immune cells in the complex tumor microenvironment (Papalexi and Satija, 2018; Stubbington et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature on scRNA-seq applications.

claim: The study reported a rare case of CRH/ACTH-secreting pheochromocytoma infiltrating the kidney and psoas muscle tissue.
source: In this study, we reported a rare case of CRH/ACTH-secreting pheochromocytoma infiltrating the kidney and psoas muscle tissue.
evidence: This is a description of the clinical case studied.

claim: POMC is a precursor for ACTH.
source: scRNA-seq identified a unique chromaffin-like cell type, called ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte, with both high expression of POMC (precursor for ACTH) and CRH pheochromocyte as well as TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, a key enzyme for catecholamine synthesization).
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge.

claim: TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) is a key enzyme for catecholamine synthesization.
source: scRNA-seq identified a unique chromaffin-like cell type, called ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte, with both high expression of POMC (precursor for ACTH) and CRH pheochromocyte as well as TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, a key enzyme for catecholamine synthesization).
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge.

claim: After tumor resection, clinical manifestations showed complete remission of CS.
source: After the tumor resection, clinical manifestations also showed complete remission of CS.
evidence: This is supported by clinical observation data.

claim: GAL encodes small neuroendocrine peptides and may be locally involved in the regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis.
source: It suggested that GAL, which encodes small neuroendocrine peptides, may be locally involved in the regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis.
evidence: This is based on data analysis and speculation about GAL function.

claim: CgA positive cells were present in both pheochromocytomas (esPHEO_T1 and PHEO_T).
source: We observed that CgA positive cells were present in both pheochromocytomas (esPHEO_T1 and PHEO_T), but ACTH positive cells were only observed in the rare pheochromocytoma (esPHEO_T1) with the ACTH-secreting cellular characteristics.
evidence: This is supported by IHC staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: ACTH positive cells were only observed in the rare pheochromocytoma (esPHEO_T1) with the ACTH-secreting cellular characteristics.
source: We observed that CgA positive cells were present in both pheochromocytomas (esPHEO_T1 and PHEO_T), but ACTH positive cells were only observed in the rare pheochromocytoma (esPHEO_T1) with the ACTH-secreting cellular characteristics.
evidence: This is supported by IHC staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: There were no CgA and ACTH positive cells in the adjacent sample (esPHEO_Adj).
source: As expected, there were no CgA and ACTH positive cells in the adjacent sample (esPHEO_Adj).
evidence: This is supported by IHC staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A total of 44,511 individual cells were analyzed after quality control filtering.
source: After quality control filtering to remove cells with low gene detection, high mitochondrial gene coverage, and doublets filtration, we compiled a unified cells-by-genes expression matrix of a total of 44,511 individual cells (Supplementary file 1, Appendix 1—figure 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data processing pipeline.

claim: The ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocytoma cell subtype was specific to three tumor samples, esPHEO_T1, esPHEO_T2, and esPHEO_T3 from Case 1.
source: The ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocytoma cell subtype was specific to three tumor samples, esPHEO_T1, esPHEO_T2, and esPHEO_T3 from Case 1, but was not observed in the peritumoral sample (esPHEO_Adj) and other adrenal tumor samples from Case 2 (PHEO_T) and Case 3 (ACA_T1 and ACA_T2).
evidence: This is supported by the scRNA-seq data analysis.

claim: The ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocytoma cell subtype was not observed in the peritumoral sample (esPHEO_Adj) and other adrenal tumor samples from Case 2 (PHEO_T) and Case 3 (ACA_T1 and ACA_T2).
source: The ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocytoma cell subtype was specific to three tumor samples, esPHEO_T1, esPHEO_T2, and esPHEO_T3 from Case 1, but was not observed in the peritumoral sample (esPHEO_Adj) and other adrenal tumor samples from Case 2 (PHEO_T) and Case 3 (ACA_T1 and ACA_T2).
evidence: This is supported by the scRNA-seq data analysis.

claim: The cell cluster of ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte was supported by the specific expression of the markers POMC (proopiomelanocortin) and CRH (corticotropin-releasing hormone).
source: The cell cluster of ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte was supported by the specific expression of the markers POMC (proopiomelanocortin) and CRH (corticotropin-releasing hormone) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: CRH is the most important regulator of ACTH secretion.
source: POMC is a precursor of ACTH, and CRH is the most important regulator of ACTH secretion.
evidence: This is established endocrinological knowledge.

claim: GAL can regulate diverse physiologic functions, including growth hormone, insulin release, and adrenal secretion.
source: GAL encodes small neuroendocrine peptides and can regulate diverse physiologic functions, including growth hormone, insulin release, and adrenal secretion (Ottlecz et al., 1988; McKnight et al., 1992; Murakami et al., 1989; Hooi et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: GAL and ACTH were co-expressed in human pituitary and pituitary adenomas.
source: A study found that GAL and ACTH were co-expressed in human pituitary and pituitary adenomas, and suggested that GAL may be locally involved in the regulation of the HPA axis (Hsu et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: GAL may be locally involved in the regulation of the HPA axis.
source: A study found that GAL and ACTH were co-expressed in human pituitary and pituitary adenomas, and suggested that GAL may be locally involved in the regulation of the HPA axis (Hsu et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: CHGA and CHGB are known adrenal chromaffin cell markers.
source: Then we examined the known adrenal chromaffin cell markers (CHGA and CHGB) and the markers for catecholamine-synthesizing enzymes (TH and PNMT) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is established knowledge about chromaffin cell markers.

claim: TH and PNMT are markers for catecholamine-synthesizing enzymes.
source: Then we examined the known adrenal chromaffin cell markers (CHGA and CHGB) and the markers for catecholamine-synthesizing enzymes (TH and PNMT) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is established knowledge about catecholamine synthesis.

claim: CHGA, CHGB, TH, PNMT, and CARTPT were observed in both ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte cell subtypes.
source: These known markers and another new candidate marker CARTPT were observed in both ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte cell subtypes.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: CYP17A1 and CYP21A2 are typical markers of the adrenal cortical cell subtype.
source: The CYP17A1 and CYP21A2, the typical markers of the adrenal cortical cell subtype, were also investigated (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is established knowledge about adrenal cortical cell markers.

claim: CYP17A1 and CYP21A2 are members of the cytochrome P450 superfamily, encoding key enzymes, and maybe the precursors of cortisol in the adrenal glucocorticoids biosynthesis pathway.
source: They are members of the cytochrome P450 superfamily, encoding key enzymes, and maybe the precursors of cortisol in the adrenal glucocorticoids biosynthesis pathway (Auchus et al., 1998; Petrunak et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature on steroid biosynthesis.

claim: Sustentacular cells were found near chromaffin cells and nerve terminations.
source: Sustentacular cells were found near chromaffin cells and nerve terminations.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Several studies have shown that sustentacular cells exhibit stem-like characteristics.
source: Several studies have shown that sustentacular cells exhibit stem-like characteristics (Pardal et al., 2007; Fitzgerald et al., 2009; Poli et al., 2019; Scriba et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The overexpression of TH and PNMT was responsible for the excessive secretion of catecholamines in the ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte cell subtypes.
source: The overexpression of TH and PNMT was responsible for the excessive secretion of catecholamines in the ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte cell subtypes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression data and knowledge of catecholamine biosynthesis.

claim: Tumor samples (esPHEO_T1, esPHEO_T2, and esPHEO_T3) from Case 1 and PHEO_T from Case 2 were demonstrated to have the function of producing catecholamine.
source: Tumor samples (esPHEO_T1, esPHEO_T2, and esPHEO_T3) from Case 1 and PHEO_T from Case 2 were demonstrated to have the function of producing catecholamine.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and clinical laboratory tests.

claim: Catecholamine-producing pheochromocytomas originated from chromaffin cells in the adrenal medulla rather than the adrenal cortex.
source: These genes related to catecholamine secretion were all negative for adrenocortical cell subtypes because the catecholamine-producing pheochromocytomas originated from chromaffin cells in the adrenal medulla rather than the adrenal cortex.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the origin of pheochromocytomas.

claim: Both Case 1 and Case 2 had a high level of catecholamines in plasma and 24 hr urine while Case 3 had a normal level.
source: Our laboratory tests were consistent with these results, that is, both Case 1 and Case 2 had a high level of catecholamines in plasma and 24 hr urine while Case 3 had a normal level.
evidence: This is supported by clinical laboratory test data.

claim: CARTPT can be used as a marker for ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte.
source: We also found CARTPT was similar to PNMT and can be used as a marker for ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data analysis.

claim: Chromaffin cell markers CHGA and CHGB were mainly characterized in PHEO_T and three tumor samples from Case 1.
source: Chromaffin cell markers CHGA and CHGB were mainly characterized in PHEO_T and three tumor samples from Case 1.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data analysis.

claim: Adrenocortical cell clusters mainly existed in ACA_T1 and ACA_T2, but a few existed in esPHEO_Adj.
source: Adrenocortical cell clusters mainly existed in ACA_T1 and ACA_T2, but a few existed in esPHEO_Adj.
evidence: This is supported by cell clustering analysis.

claim: S100B was specifically identified in PHEO_T.
source: S100B was specifically identified in PHEO_T.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data analysis.

claim: An absence of S100-positive sustentacular cells has been previously confirmed in most malignant adrenal pheochromocytomas.
source: An absence of S100-positive sustentacular cells has been previously confirmed in most malignant adrenal pheochromocytomas, and the locally aggressive or recurrent group usually contains a large number of these cells (Unger et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The locally aggressive or recurrent group of pheochromocytomas usually contains a large number of S100-positive sustentacular cells.
source: An absence of S100-positive sustentacular cells has been previously confirmed in most malignant adrenal pheochromocytomas, and the locally aggressive or recurrent group usually contains a large number of these cells (Unger et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: PHEO_T from Case 2 might be a locally aggressive case, while Case 1 is the opposite.
source: It suggests that PHEO_T from Case 2 might be a locally aggressive case, while Case 1 is the opposite.
evidence: This is an inference based on the presence/absence of S100-positive cells and previous literature.

claim: Immunofluorescence co-staining showed legible co-localization signals for POMC&CRH and POMC&TH.
source: The legible co-localization signals were observed, where the green signal was for POMC, and the red signal was for CRH and TH (Figure 3E, Appendix 1—figure 9).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Many genes were dramatically upregulated specifically in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte when compared with the other tumor cell types, such as GAL, POMC, PNMT, and CARTPT.
source: It is worth noting that many genes were dramatically upregulated specifically in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte when compared with the other tumor cell types, such as GAL, POMC, PNMT, and CARTPT (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In comparison with adrenocortical cell types, the highly upregulated genes of ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte were mainly enriched in the neuropeptide signaling pathway, hormone secretion, and transport.
source: In comparison with adrenocortical cell types, the highly upregulated genes of ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte were mainly enriched in the neuropeptide signaling pathway, hormone secretion, and transport, while the downregulated genes were mostly enriched in the pathway of adrenocortical hormones (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by GO functional enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The downregulated genes in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte compared to adrenocortical cell types were mostly enriched in the pathway of adrenocortical hormones.
source: In comparison with adrenocortical cell types, the highly upregulated genes of ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte were mainly enriched in the neuropeptide signaling pathway, hormone secretion, and transport, while the downregulated genes were mostly enriched in the pathway of adrenocortical hormones (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by GO functional enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Comparing the two types of pheochromocyte, the upregulated genes for ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte were enriched in the neuropeptide signaling pathway.
source: Comparing the two types of pheochromocyte, GO functional enrichment analysis for the biology process (BP) revealed that the upregulated genes for ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte were also enriched in the neuropeptide signaling pathway, while the enrichment of the downregulated genes from the GO functional result hardly reach statistical significance.
evidence: This is supported by GO functional enrichment analysis.

claim: A total of 248 upregulated and 198 downregulated genes were detected in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte compared with adrenocortical cells.
source: Interestingly, compared with adrenocortical cells, a total of 248 upregulated and 198 downregulated genes were detected in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte, while only 95 upregulated and 111 downregulated genes were detected in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte when compared with pheochromocyte (Figure 4C), which suggested that the difference between ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte was relatively small.
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Only 95 upregulated and 111 downregulated genes were detected in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte when compared with pheochromocyte.
source: Interestingly, compared with adrenocortical cells, a total of 248 upregulated and 198 downregulated genes were detected in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte, while only 95 upregulated and 111 downregulated genes were detected in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte when compared with pheochromocyte (Figure 4C), which suggested that the difference between ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte was relatively small.
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The difference between ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte was relatively small.
source: Interestingly, compared with adrenocortical cells, a total of 248 upregulated and 198 downregulated genes were detected in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte, while only 95 upregulated and 111 downregulated genes were detected in ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte when compared with pheochromocyte (Figure 4C), which suggested that the difference between ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte and pheochromocyte was relatively small.
evidence: This is an inference based on the number of differentially expressed genes.

claim: PNMT catalyzes the last step of the catecholamine biosynthesis pathway, methylating norepinephrine to form epinephrine.
source: Of which, the product of PNMT catalyzes the last step of the catecholamine biosynthesis pathway, methylating norepinephrine to form epinephrine.
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge.

claim: The overexpression of PNMT was responsible for the significantly elevated epinephrine of the rare Case 1 with ectopic ACTH and CRH secretory pheochromocytoma.
source: The overexpression of PNMT was responsible for the signiﬁcantly elevated epinephrine (Appendix 1—table 1) of the rare Case 1 with ectopic ACTH and CRH secretory pheochromocytoma.
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression data and clinical laboratory results.

claim: The rare Case 1 harbor the ACTH-dependent CS is due to the presence of the identified novel tumor cell type of ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte, which secretes both ACTH and CRH.
source: Furthermore, we believed that the rare Case 1 harbor the ACTH-dependent CS is due to the presence of the identified novel tumor cell type of ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte, which secretes both ACTH and CRH.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data analysis and clinical observations.

claim: Sustentacular cells were in an early state in pseudotime analysis.
source: The sustentacular cells were in an early state in pseudotime analysis (Figure 6A, B and C), which was in accordance with their exhibited stem-like properties and the highest unspliced proportion among non-immune cell types in the RNA velocity analysis.
evidence: This is supported by pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The results showed a transition from sustentacular cells to pheochromocytes and then to ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte, and adrenocortical cells were on another branch.
source: The results also showed a transition from sustentacular cells to pheochromocytes and then to ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocyte, and adrenocortical cells were on another branch (Figure 6A, B and C).
evidence: This is supported by pseudotime trajectory analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Immune cells accounted for more than ~50% of total cells.
source: Analysis of our transcriptional profiles revealed that from the frequency distribution of cell clusters, immune cells accounted for more than ~50% of total cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by cell clustering analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All three tumor specimens and one peritumoral specimen from the rare case had similar immune cell composition due to the identical tumor microenvironment.
source: Due to the identical tumor microenvironment, all three tumor specimens one peritumoral specimen from the rare case had similar immune cell composition.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immune cell composition data.

claim: CD4 T cells, B cells, and macrophages are mainly presented in two adrenal cortical adenomas (ACA_T1 and ACA_T2).
source: Interestingly, the CD4 T cells, B cells, and macrophages are mainly presented in two adrenal cortical adenomas (ACA_T1 and ACA_T2), while the CD8 T cells mostly resided in the microenvironment of other pheochromocytoma tumor and the peritumoral specimen.
evidence: This is supported by immune cell composition analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: CD8 T cells mostly resided in the microenvironment of other pheochromocytoma tumor and the peritumoral specimen.
source: Interestingly, the CD4 T cells, B cells, and macrophages are mainly presented in two adrenal cortical adenomas (ACA_T1 and ACA_T2), while the CD8 T cells mostly resided in the microenvironment of other pheochromocytoma tumor and the peritumoral specimen.
evidence: This is supported by immune cell composition analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Compared with CD4 T cells in adrenocortical adenomas, the pheochromocytoma types were mostly manifested by activated CD8+, especially in the anatomic specimens from the ectopic ACTH&CRH secreting pheochromocytoma.
source: We found the heterogeneity of T cells in different adrenal tumor subtypes, that is, compared with CD4 T cells in adrenocortical adenomas, the pheochromocytoma types were mostly manifested by activated CD8+, especially in the anatomic specimens from the ectopic ACTH&CRH secreting pheochromocytoma.
evidence: This is supported by immune cell composition analysis.

claim: Endothelial cells consisted of four distinct sub-clusters: vascular endothelial cells, lymphatic endothelial cells, cortical endothelial cells, and other endothelial cells.
source: Endothelial cells consisted of four distinct sub-clusters: vascular endothelial cells, lymphatic endothelial cells, cortical endothelial cells, and other endothelial cells, as shown in the cell cluster distribution map highlighted by endothelial cells (Figure 8A, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by cell clustering analysis shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Vascular endothelial cells were mainly identified in pheochromocytoma samples (esPHEO_T1, esPHEO_T2, esPHEO_T3, and PHEO_T).
source: Vascular endothelial cells were mainly identified in pheochromocytoma samples (esPHEO_T1, esPHEO_T2, esPHEO_T3, and PHEO_T), because pheochromocytoma is a tumor arising in the adrenal medulla, and vascular endothelial cells might be detected from the medullary capillary.
evidence: This is supported by endothelial cell composition analysis shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Pheochromocytoma is a tumor arising in the adrenal medulla.
source: Vascular endothelial cells were mainly identified in pheochromocytoma samples (esPHEO_T1, esPHEO_T2, esPHEO_T3, and PHEO_T), because pheochromocytoma is a tumor arising in the adrenal medulla, and vascular endothelial cells might be detected from the medullary capillary.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge.

claim: Cortical endothelial cells were mainly detected in adrenocortical adenomas (ACA_T1 and ACA_T2).
source: Cortical endothelial cells were mainly detected in adrenocortical adenomas (ACA_T1 and ACA_T2).
evidence: This is supported by endothelial cell composition analysis shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Lymphatic endothelial cells were found in the adjacent adrenal specimen of the rare ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocytoma (esPHEO_Adj).
source: Lymphatic endothelial cells were found in the adjacent adrenal specimen of the rare ACTH+&CRH + pheochromocytoma (esPHEO_Adj).
evidence: This is supported by endothelial cell composition analysis shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Vascular endothelial cells are the barrier between the blood and vascular wall and have the functions of organizing the extracellular matrix and regulating the metabolism of vasoactive substances.
source: Vascular endothelial cells are the barrier between the blood and vascular wall and have the functions of organizing the extracellular matrix and regulating the metabolism of vasoactive substances.
evidence: This is established knowledge about vascular endothelial cell function.

claim: Lymphatic endothelial cells are responsible for chemokine-mediated pathways.
source: Lymphatic endothelial cells are responsible for chemokine-mediated pathways.
evidence: This is based on GO functional enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Cortical endothelial cells express TFF3 and FABP4, which are involved in repairing and maintaining stable functions.
source: Cortical endothelial cells express TFF3 and FABP4, which are involved in repairing and maintaining stable functions.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data and GO functional enrichment analysis.

claim: Surgery is the most common treatment strategy for ectopic ACTH&CRH secreting pheochromocytoma.
source: Surgery is the most common treatment strategy for this type of tumor.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge.

claim: The molecular mechanism of CS in Case 3 was different, which was attributed to two cortical adenomas on the left adrenal, showing ACTH-independent hypercortisolemia.
source: The molecular mechanism of CS in Case 3 was different, which was attributed to two cortical adenomas on the left adrenal, showing ACTH-independent hypercortisolemia.
evidence: This is based on clinical observations and data analysis.

claim: Genetic mutations of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma are mainly classified into two major clusters, that is, pseudo hypoxic pathway and kinase signaling pathways.
source: Genetic mutations of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma are mainly classified into two major clusters, that is, pseudo hypoxic pathway and kinase signaling pathways (Pillai et al., 2016; Nölting and Grossman, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: No gene mutations related to the two major clusters of pheochromocytoma were found in the rare case.
source: We did not find any gene mutations that were related to these two major clusters.
evidence: This is based on whole-exome sequencing data analysis.

claim: One shared somatic variant of ACAN (c.5951T > A:p.L1984Q) was identified comparing variants in tumor samples to controls.
source: We only identified one shared somatic variant of ACAN (c.5951T > A:p.L1984Q) comparing variants in tumor samples to controls but Sanger sequencing only confirmed the presence in esPHEO_T3 which was not observed in esPHEO_T2 (Appendix 1—figure 7).
evidence: This is based on whole-exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing validation.

claim: ACAN encodes a major component of the extracellular matrix and is a member of the aggrecan/versican proteoglycan family.
source: ACAN, encoding a major component of the extracellular matrix, is a member of the aggrecan/versican proteoglycan family.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the ACAN gene.

claim: Mutations of ACAN were reported related to steroid levels.
source: Mutations of ACAN were reported related to steroid levels (Yousri et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: No obvious genetic driver was found to explain the rare case of ACTH/CRH-secreting phaeochromocytoma.
source: Therefore, no obvious genetic driver was found to explain the rare case of ACTH/CRH-secreting phaeochromocytoma.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the whole-exome sequencing analysis.

claim: Dale's Principle states 'one cell, one hormone, and one neuron one transmitter'.
source: For many years, the understanding of neurotransmission has been dominated by the concept of 'one cell, one hormone, and one neuron one transmitter,' which is known as Dale's Principle (Dale in 1934; for detailed discussion, see Burnstock, 1976; Burnstock, 1976).
evidence: This is a historical scientific principle with citations.

claim: Sakuma et al., 2016 reported an ectopic ACTH pheochromocytoma case and proved that ACTH and catecholamine were produced by two functionally distinct chromaffin-like tumor cell types through immunohistochemical analysis.
source: Sakuma et al., 2016 reported an ectopic ACTH pheochromocytoma case and proved that ACTH and catecholamine were produced by two functionally distinct chromaffin-like tumor cell types through immunohistochemical analysis Sakuma et al., 2016.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: More and more evidence has emerged that Dale's principle is incorrect because existing studies have shown that these cells are multi-messenger systems.
source: However, more and more evidence has emerged that Dale's principle is incorrect because existing studies have shown that these cells are multi-messenger systems (Hakanson and Sundler, 1983; Apergis-Schoute et al., 2019; Svensson et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Adrenal glands are composed of two main tissue types, namely, the cortex and the medulla, which are responsible for producing steroid and catecholamine hormones, respectively.
source: Adrenal glands are composed of two main tissue types, namely, the cortex and the medulla, which are responsible for producing steroid and catecholamine hormones, respectively.
evidence: This is established anatomical and physiological knowledge.

claim: The inner medulla is derived from neuroectodermal cells of neural crest origin, while the outer cortex is derived from the intermediate mesoderm.
source: The inner medulla is derived from neuroectodermal cells of neural crest origin, while the outer cortex is derived from the intermediate mesoderm.
evidence: This is established developmental biology knowledge.

claim: Sustentacular cells were absent in most malignant pheochromocytomas.
source: By evaluating 17 malignant and recurrent or locally aggressive adrenal pheochromocytomas, Unger et al., 1991 found that sustentacular cells were absent in most malignant cases (Unger et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: ACTH&CRH secreting pheochromocytoma is more serious than the common pheochromocytoma because there are no sustentacular cells.
source: Because there are no sustentacular cells in ACTH&CRH secreting pheochromocytoma, ACTH&CRH secreting pheochromocytoma is more serious than the common pheochromocytoma.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of sustentacular cells and previous literature.

claim: A unique case of a tumor originating from S100-positive sustentacular cells was previously reported.
source: A unique case of a tumor originating from S100-positive sustentacular cells was previously reported (Lau et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The RNA velocity estimation and pseudo-time analysis of different adrenal cell subtypes supported the sustentacular cells exhibiting stem-like properties.
source: The RNA velocity estimation and pseudo-time analysis of different adrenal cell subtypes supported the sustentacular cells exhibiting stem-like properties.
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity and pseudotime analysis data.

claim: ACTH&CRH secreting pheochromocyte have more hormone-producing functions and retain stem- and endocrine-differentiation ability.
source: We assumed that ACTH&CRH secreting pheochromocyte have more hormone-producing functions, retain stem- and endocrine-diﬀerentiation ability.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the data analysis.

claim: There are bidirectional communications between the immune system and the neuroendocrine system.
source: There are bidirectional communications between the immune system and the neuroendocrine system (Blalock, 1989).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Hormones produced in the endocrine system, especially glucocorticoids, affect the immune system to modulate its function.
source: Hormones produced in the endocrine system, especially glucocorticoids, affect the immune system to modulate its function (Imura and Fukata, 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Growth hormone (GH) and prolactin (PRL) modulate the immune system.
source: Other hormones, such as growth hormone (GH) and prolactin (PRL), also modulate the immune system (Blalock, 1989).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The exogenous production of cytokines can stimulate and mediate the release of multiple hormones including ACTH and CRH.
source: It has been proved that the exogenous production of cytokines can stimulate and mediate the release of multiple hormones including ACTH, CRH (Rivier et al., 1989; Bernton et al., 1987), and induce the activation of the HPA axis (Gisslinger et al., 1993; Fukata et al., 1994; Kakucska et al., 1993; Murakami N Fukata et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cytokines can induce the activation of the HPA axis.
source: It has been proved that the exogenous production of cytokines can stimulate and mediate the release of multiple hormones including ACTH, CRH (Rivier et al., 1989; Bernton et al., 1987), and induce the activation of the HPA axis (Gisslinger et al., 1993; Fukata et al., 1994; Kakucska et al., 1993; Murakami N Fukata et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Human T cells coordinate the adaptive immunity of different anatomic compartments by producing cytokines and effector molecules.
source: Human T cells coordinate the adaptive immunity of different anatomic compartments by producing cytokines and effector molecules (Szabo et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The activation of naive T cells through the antigen-specific T cell receptor (TCR) can initiate transcriptional programs that can drive the differentiation of lineage-specific effector functions.
source: The activation of naive T cells through the antigen-specific T cell receptor (TCR) can initiate transcriptional programs that can drive the differentiation of lineage-specific effector functions.
evidence: This is established immunological knowledge.

claim: CD4+ T cells secrete cytokines to recruit and activate other immune cells.
source: CD4+ T cells secrete cytokines to recruit and activate other immune cells, while CD8+ T cells have cytotoxic functions and can directly kill infected or tumor cells.
evidence: This is established immunological knowledge.

claim: CD8+ T cells have cytotoxic functions and can directly kill infected or tumor cells.
source: CD4+ T cells secrete cytokines to recruit and activate other immune cells, while CD8+ T cells have cytotoxic functions and can directly kill infected or tumor cells.
evidence: This is established immunological knowledge.

claim: The composition of the T cell subset is related to the specific tissue locations.
source: Recent studies have shown that the composition of the T cell subset is related to the specific tissue locations (Carpenter et al., 2018; Thome et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Signaling through IL-7R is essential in the developmental process and regulation of lymphoid cells.
source: Previous studies have shown that signaling through IL-7R is essential in the developmental process and regulation of lymphoid cells (Kondrack et al., 2003; Tan et al., 2001; Tan et al., 2002; Lenz et al., 2004; Li et al., 2003; Seddon et al., 2003), and disruption of the IL-7R signaling pathway may lead to skewed T cell distribution and cause immunodeficiency (Maraskovsky et al., 1996; Kaech et al., 2003; Carini et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Disruption of the IL-7R signaling pathway may lead to skewed T cell distribution and cause immunodeficiency.
source: Previous studies have shown that signaling through IL-7R is essential in the developmental process and regulation of lymphoid cells (Kondrack et al., 2003; Tan et al., 2001; Tan et al., 2002; Lenz et al., 2004; Li et al., 2003; Seddon et al., 2003), and disruption of the IL-7R signaling pathway may lead to skewed T cell distribution and cause immunodeficiency (Maraskovsky et al., 1996; Kaech et al., 2003; Carini et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CD4+ T cells with the high expression level of IL-7R might be related to adrenal tumor progression, apoptosis, or factors influencing progression such as immune activation.
source: Our results indicated the heterogeneity of the immune system between different samples, and CD4+ T cells with the high expression level of IL-7R might be related to adrenal tumor progression, apoptosis, or factors influencing progression such as immune activation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data analysis and previous literature.

claim: Sustentacular cells exhibit high proportions of unspliced/spliced transcripts.
source: We observed the ratios of spliced and unspliced mRNA, and sustentacular cell type was ranking first with 36% unspliced proportions among non-immune cell types (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is supported by RNA velocity analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The balance of unspliced and spliced mRNA abundance is an indicator of the future state of mature mRNA abundance, and thus the future state of the cell.
source: The balance of unspliced and spliced mRNA abundance is an indicator of the future state of mature mRNA abundance, and thus the future state of the cell (Bergen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the RNA velocity methodology paper.

claim: Unspliced transcripts were enriched in genes involved in DNA binding and RNA processing in hematopoietic stem cells.
source: Previously study had observed unspliced transcripts were enriched in genes involved in DNA binding and RNA processing in hematopoietic stem cells (Bowman et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: There were more spliced transcripts proportions in POMC+&CRH + pheochromocytes than in pheochromocytes.
source: There were more spliced transcripts proportions in POMC+&CRH + pheochromocytes than in pheochromocytes (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by RNA velocity analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: From velocity streamlines, the four adrenal cell subtypes (POMC+&CRH + pheochromocytes, pheochromocytes adrenocortical cells, and sustentacular cells) were independent respectively and not directed toward other cell types.
source: From velocity streamlines, we found the four adrenal cell subtypes, that is, POMC+&CRH + pheochromocytes, pheochromocytes adrenocortical cells, and sustentacular cells, were independent respectively and not directed toward other cell types (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by RNA velocity streamline analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Genes like POMC and CRH only contain one coding sequence (CDS) region and were all detected as spliced.
source: Genes, like POMC and CRH, only contain one coding sequence (CDS) region, were all detected as spliced (Appendix 1—figure 5).
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis.

claim: The actual values of RNA velocity for POMC+&CRH + pheochromocytes might be larger than the predicted ones.
source: It indicated that the actual values of RNA velocity for POMC+&CRH + pheochromocytes might be larger than the predicted ones.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that POMC and CRH are detected as spliced.

claim: The spliced versus unspliced phase for CHGA, CHGB, and TH demonstrated a clear more dynamics expression in POMC+&CRH + pheochromocytes than in pheochromocytes.
source: Furthermore, the spliced versus unspliced phase for CHGA, CHGB, and TH demonstrated a clear more dynamics expression in POMC+&CRH + pheochromocytes than in pheochromocytes (Appendix 1—figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by RNA velocity phase analysis.

claim: Medullary cells are earlier than cortical cells in pseudotime.
source: As observed in the pseudotime of four adrenal cell subtypes, medullary cells are earlier than cortical cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 5C.
